docs.summary:
Supplies the height grid and where it sits in the world.

The grid itself is defined in terrain-local space: cell (x,z) sits at `(x, height, z) * CellSize` with no rotation, scale or offset baked in. [`LocalToWorld`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.ITerrainHeightProvider~LocalToWorld) carries all of that, which is what lets terrain be rotated arbitrarily - queries are brought into local space, walked on the axis-aligned grid there, and their results taken back out.

members.name: TryGetHeight
members.signature: bool TryGetHeight(int x, int z, out float height)

docs.summary: Height at integer grid coordinates, in terrain-local units. Scale and world offset are not applied here; they come from [`LocalToWorld`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.ITerrainHeightProvider~LocalToWorld).
docs.returns: True if the coordinates are valid and height was retrieved.

docs.summary: Whether a cell exists. Cells are indexed 0..Width-2 and 0..Height-2, one per quad.
Check if a cell is a hole (should skip collision). Default false.
Number of height samples along X.
Number of height samples along Z.
Spacing between height samples, in terrain-local units.

Terrain-local to world, carrying position, rotation and scale. Read per query, so the terrain can be moved, turned or scaled after registration; cached on the main thread by the implementation, because the broad phase samples it from worker threads.
The inverse of [`LocalToWorld`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.ITerrainHeightProvider~LocalToWorld), for bringing world queries into the grid.
World-space bounds enclosing the terrain at its full height range, rotation included.

members.name: TryGetCellRange
members.signature: bool TryGetCellRange(in JBoundingBox worldBounds, out int minX, out int minZ, out int maxX, out int maxZ)

docs.summary:
The range of cells a world-space bounding box could touch, clamped to the grid. Upper bounds are exclusive, so callers iterate `x < maxX`.

The box is brought into local space corner by corner and re-bounded there, because a rotated terrain turns an axis-aligned world box into an oriented one. Re-bounding is conservative, which is what a broad-phase range has to be.
docs.returns: False when the box cannot touch the grid at all.

members.name: TryGetWorldCorners
members.signature: bool TryGetWorldCorners(int x, int z, out JVector a, out JVector b, out JVector c, out JVector d)

docs.summary: The four world-space corners of one cell, laid out as `a`=(x,z), `b`=(x+1,z), `c`=(x+1,z+1), `d`=(x,z+1).
docs.returns: False when any corner has no height, so the cell should be skipped.
